amount_tolerance.rule: tolerance = max(flat, percent * invoice_amount), percent portion rounded to cents (ROUND_HALF_UP); a pair matches on amount iff abs(payment.amount - invoice.amount) <= tolerance

date_window.rule: a pair matches on date iff abs((payment.payment_date - invoice.due_date).days) <= days

assumptions.payment_row_index: 0-based index into payments_csv's data rows (excluding the header row); stable because row order is fixed at generation time and never shuffled.

scenarios.description: Exact match on amount, date, and reference.
scenarios.notes: Baseline clean_match case: amount, payment date (== due date), and reference text all agree exactly.

scenarios.description: Payment is exactly $1.00 below invoice amount; flat tolerance binds (0.5% of $80 is only $0.40).
scenarios.notes: Tolerance = max($1.00, 0.5% * $80.00) = $1.00. Diff is exactly $1.00 -- at the boundary, should match.

scenarios.description: Payment is $1.01 below invoice amount -- one cent past the flat tolerance boundary.
scenarios.notes: Tolerance = $1.00; diff is $1.01, one cent past it. Must NOT match. Date and reference otherwise agree exactly, so 'amount_mismatch_only' is the advisory expected exception reason (Task 5 owns the final exception-classification logic).

scenarios.description: Payment is exactly $50.00 below invoice amount; percentage tolerance binds (0.5% of $10,000 is $50, more than the $1 flat).
scenarios.notes: Tolerance = max($1.00, 0.5% * $10,000.00) = $50.00. Diff is exactly $50.00 -- at the boundary, should match.

scenarios.description: Payment is $50.01 below invoice amount -- one cent past the percentage tolerance boundary.
scenarios.notes: Tolerance = $50.00; diff is $50.01, one cent past it. Must NOT match.

scenarios.description: Payment lands exactly 5 days after the invoice due date (the assumed default window boundary).
scenarios.notes: Amount and reference exact; payment_date - due_date == 5 days, the boundary -- should match.

scenarios.description: Payment lands 6 days after the invoice due date -- one day past the window.
scenarios.notes: Amount and reference exact; payment_date - due_date == 6 days, one day past the 5-day window. Must NOT match. 'below_threshold' is an advisory expected exception reason.

scenarios.description: Payment memo references a typo'd invoice number (digits transposed: 1410 instead of 1401).
scenarios.notes: Amount and date exact; reference is a near-miss fuzzy match (transposed digits) plus an exact vendor name -- should still match.

scenarios.description: Payment memo contains the vendor name with its words reordered and no invoice number.
scenarios.notes: Amount and date exact; reference text is a token-reordered variant of the vendor name -- should still match via fuzzy token matching.

scenarios.description: Payment references an abbreviated vendor name (IBM) instead of the full legal name.
scenarios.notes: Amount and date exact; vendor is abbreviated to its common initialism and the invoice number has no hyphen -- should still match.

scenarios.description: Payment has an empty memo and a generic, non-identifying counterparty -- no usable reference text at all.
scenarios.notes: Amount and date exact; reference/counterparty carry no identifying signal (expected reference_score ~= 0), so the match must be inferable from amount + date alone.

scenarios.description: Invoice with no corresponding payment anywhere in the dataset.
scenarios.notes: True orphan invoice: never paid.

scenarios.description: Bank transaction with no corresponding invoice (a refund).
scenarios.notes: True orphan payment: a refund/unrelated transaction that was never invoiced.

scenarios.description: Two invoices with identical amount and due date; one payment with a generic reference fits either equally well.
scenarios.notes: INV-1701 and INV-1702 are identical on amount/date/vendor; the payment's reference does not favor either. Must not auto-match; expect an ambiguous-candidates exception listing both as candidates.

scenarios.description: Payment amount is exactly half of the invoice amount; reference and date otherwise agree.
scenarios.notes: Despite an exact reference/date match, the amount is only half of the invoice and far outside tolerance. Must NOT auto-match as a full payment.

scenarios.description: Invoice amount equals the sum of two separate payments, neither of which individually matches it.
scenarios.notes: $600 + $600 == $1,200, but neither payment individually is within tolerance of the invoice. Neither should auto-match.

scenarios.description: Two payments with the same amount and the same day, but different references, correctly resolving to two distinct invoices.
scenarios.notes: The amount+date collision could look like a duplicate payment to a matcher that only looks at amount/date, but the references clearly disambiguate: both are legitimate, distinct clean-ish matches and both should match.
